cells.tense: Right now you are at the bench in your life where things get weighed fairly, and you meet it still able to wonder.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Find something close by that already sits fair, and feed it a little on purpose — some warmth, some attention, ten minutes — without checking whether it pays off. Come back to it tomorrow if you feel like it.
cells.core:
You can stand at the scales and still be turned toward what hasn't happened yet — the fairness you keep in play here is steady, and the feeling under it is genuine. Nothing forced in that. What sits out of true gets noticed and adjusted, and you don't have to manufacture caring to do it. High in your range, wonder is allowed to move you, and things come out more level for it, not less. People at that edge tend to go flat and guarded. You don't.

This balance has a next thing it's free to feed, and it's yours: keep a fire going under one small piece of it, steadily, without measuring returns. Warmth first, a little, then more tomorrow. The scales don't need the extra attention — the steady part does, and what you're carrying gets held longer when the drive is fed in small amounts.
cells.sheetLine: You can still be moved by wonder while keeping things fair.
cells.verb: meeting what is not yet here with fresh wonder
cells.place: where what is owed gets weighed and set level

cells.tense: You will have the fairness sorted ahead of time, which is how a corner of life stops getting to arrive as itself.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Watch over something small and real — a plant, a pot, a routine — on the schedule it keeps, for a week. Give it what it needs and nothing extra, and notice what that teaches you.
cells.core:
Ahead of you, this ground is being set even now — who gets what, what it means, how it should come out — and wonder is doing the weighing. It's a fair structure and it's drawn too tight. What hasn't happened yet doesn't get to show up as itself; it shows up already measured, already apportioned, and you're holding the rule. That's what the bracing does. From where you stand it reads as careful.

There's a slower move that lets the balance come back by itself: care for one actual thing, small, and pick up what it needs at the pace it moves. Fresh hands, no steering the outcome, no fixing the speed. Slower than the rule, and that's the point — you're going to want to decide how it goes, and it won't. Give it a week and see what the learning does to how you hold what comes next.
cells.sheetLine: You are apportioning what hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: meeting what is not yet here with fresh wonder
cells.place: where what is owed gets weighed and set level

cells.tense: Where fairness lives in your circumstances, the session was called and you were somewhere else, and you have not been back since.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Take one question you truly don't know the answer to, and follow it for twenty minutes with no outcome in mind. Read it, ask someone, sit with it. Then stop.
cells.core:
In this corner of things, the scales stopped being touched by feeling; the dreaming that used to move you sat down and hasn't stood back up. You've been reading the situation from behind yourself — accurate, watchful, not really in it — and fair weighing is something you watch others attempt, not something you're actively doing. The gift is still there. It's just not running.

You won't get it back by measuring harder; effort into that bench is the last thing it needs. Give the charge to something else instead: chase a question with no use for it. Not to be fair, not to be right — because you want to know. The curiosity is the instrument and the odds are it lands without argument, once the answer isn't the point. That's the same thing the scales run on, coming back through the eyes.
cells.sheetLine: The scales stopped being touched. You've been keeping them at a distance.

cells.tense: You are balancing this ground right now, and if asked, you would put the steadiness down to the situation.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Pick something you're balancing and set down, plainly, what you actually take in about it — what you see, what's off. No feeling words. Then follow the page to the question worth asking.
cells.core:
Whatever is being held level here is being held by you — the calibrating, the catching when something sits wrong, the drawing on feeling that keeps you turned toward it. You'd file it under circumstance. Circumstance didn't do it. And running underneath is a steadier method than you'd give yourself credit for: this ground could stand a known, plain discipline, and it would grow from being held to one instead of being read raw anew each pass.

So set down the facts of one situation in order, without feeling words, and follow the line where it goes. Not a journal — an inquiry. It doesn't need to move anyone. It needs to be seen through once, and the discipline is what you have standing by: practice without forcing, solitude that connects rather than isolates. What you've been quietly attending to gets an author, and the balance you've been keeping stops looking like something that just happened.
cells.sheetLine: You keep this balanced and file it under circumstance.
cells.verb: meeting what is not yet here with fresh wonder
cells.place: where what is owed gets weighed and set level

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's sense of proportion is currently being bent by the same imagination that is set to serve it — the record shows both capacities present, not that one is causing trouble here. A reader could say the bracing is simply ordinary event-planning and the fairness instinct is fine. The asks survive being wrong because each one is an act of the partner's own medicine done small, useful regardless of whether the mechanism I named is what's running. The sentence that serves me more than the person is any clause like 'when wonder turns on what people owe you' — it sounds sharp and says less than the plain thing, so it is cut.
